description: The model inventory record beside the receipts and the signed deployment manifest: the layout its strict reader reads, the bound and asserted fields the layout keeps apart, the pointer registry it enumerates, and the limits sentence every record states verbatim. The fixture deployment is the one the published receipt family came from, stated by the manifest row paired-with-the-published-receipt-family; the bound fields are copied from that row's payload and the asserted fields are the fixture deployer's statements, so the extract is labeled fixture and describes no live deployment. The parse rows carry the record bytes the shipped writer made, or one edit of them at the position the fault names; the bound cases carry the record beside the manifest bytes it designates and the verdict the verifying door owes the pair, including the mutation pair that witnesses the split: a bound mutation refused and an asserted mutation read. The export ride publishes the record as one inline item of the published export container, which no member of that contract moves for.

pointerCitations.osfi-e23-app-1: OSFI E-23 (model risk management guideline), Appendix 1

rule.limits: This record is an inventory extract, not a legal determination. Its bound fields are copied from the deployment manifest it designates and are checked against that manifest when a reader is handed it; its asserted fields are the deployment's own statements, which nothing in this record proves. The pointers name provisions for counsel to weigh, not conclusions that a duty applies or was met. A record labeled fixture describes fixture material and no live deployment.

manifest.note: The sealed manifest the honest record designates, byte for byte the row the manifest family publishes, beside the key that family publishes as signing the manifests a reader designates. A bound case carries its own manifest bytes, so a port replays each pair without reaching into another family.

exportRide.note: The record as one inline item of a plain export signed by the fixture receipt key. verifyExport checks the item's digest; the item's original bytes are the record bytes, read back through both inventory doors. The export contract moves no member for the inventory.

rule.encodings: byte strings unpadded base64url, digests lowercase hex, instants unix seconds

vectors.name: inventory-fixture-v1
vectors.note: A whole record over the fixture deployment: the bound model id and weights digest copied from the paired manifest row, the asserted version, purpose, risk category and review stated by the fixture deployer, the three counsel pointers, and the format's limits sentence verbatim. The provenance is fixture, so the record labels itself as describing fixture material.

vectors.name: inventory-unknown-member-v1
vectors.note: A well-formed record carrying one member the top level does not define. The layout closes every map it declares, so an unknown member is a malformed document rather than a member a reader agreed to forget.

fault.states: a top-level member the layout does not define

vectors.name: inventory-unknown-model-member-v1
vectors.note: A well-formed record whose model entry carries a member the entry does not define, beside the six it does. The closure rule reaches the maps inside the list, so a weights path no member of this layout holds is refused at the entry that carries it.

fault.states: a model member the layout does not define

vectors.name: inventory-limits-reworded-v1
vectors.note: A record wording its own limits. The limits are the format's sentence, verbatim, and a record widening or narrowing them is a document of a shape the layout does not define: the one thing a reader must not have to weigh is whether the record's own account of its limits is true.

fault.states: a limits sentence the format does not own

vectors.name: inventory-unknown-pointer-v1
vectors.note: A well-formed record whose pointers name a provision outside the registry: a near miss of the OSFI appendix pointer rather than a label no instrument resembles. The document is whole and it is the provision it names that this reader has no pointer for, which is the refusal MODEL_INVENTORY_UNKNOWN_POINTER exists for, apart from a malformed document.

fault.states: a label the pointer registry does not hold

vectors.name: inventory-empty-models-v1
vectors.note: A record whose models list is empty. An inventory of no models states nothing about what ran, the same refusal the pack arrives at for an empty items array: a document whose own figures are vacuous reads as evidence while attesting nothing.

fault.states: the non-empty list the layout requires, emptied

vectors.name: inventory-review-after-assembly-v1
vectors.note: A record whose single review is stamped one second after the extract's own assembly stamp. Both instants are inside one record, so a review postdating the extract that carries it is another document's review, the same rule the export's claim states beside the assembly stamp.

fault.states: a review stamp after the extract that carries it

vectors.name: inventory-duplicate-model-v1
vectors.note: A record naming one model twice. Two entries answering to one id make a refusal name whichever of the two a reader happened to meet first, and every statement the record makes about a model is made once per model the deployment ran.

fault.states: the model id models[0] already names

vectors.name: inventory-version-two-v1
vectors.note: A record declaring a version nothing has published. The version is asked before any member is read, because which member list applies is the one question a wrong version cannot be talked out of.

fault.states: a version no layout this package reads defines

vectors.name: inventory-member-named-twice-v1
vectors.note: The writer's bytes with the version member written a second time, the two spellings identical. JSON.parse would keep the last and say nothing while the bytes carry both, so the strict reading refuses the document while the characters are still distinguishable.

fault.states: the member name v, stated twice in the file's own text

vectors.name: inventory-float-stamp-v1
vectors.note: The assembly stamp written as a fraction that equals the integer it imitates. By the time a field check could ask which spelling the writer chose the two are one JavaScript number, so the reading refuses the spelling rather than the value.

fault.states: a number written as a fraction where the layout holds an integer

boundCases.name: bound-honest-sealed-authenticated
boundCases.note: The honest record verified against the sealed manifest it designates, under the key the manifest family publishes for that purpose. The bound fields agree with the manifest's own declaration and the outcome reports the seal authenticated.

boundCases.name: bound-honest-sealed-unauthenticated
boundCases.note: The same pair with no key designated. The digest and the bound fields are still checked, and the outcome reports the authentication the reader did not do rather than implying one: a sealed manifest read without a key is a document whose signer nobody vouched for.

boundCases.name: bound-honest-plain
boundCases.note: A record designating the plain payload bytes rather than the seal, verified against those bytes. The designation is over the exact bytes handed over, so the two shapes a deployment serves are two designations and not one shape preferred.

boundCases.name: bound-plain-under-designated-key
boundCases.note: The plain document beside a designated manifest signing key. The caller stated a demand about who may sign the manifest and an unsigned document does not meet it, which is a refusal about the designation rather than about bytes that may be a whole manifest.

boundCases.name: bound-other-manifest
boundCases.note: The honest record beside the manifest family's other deployment, sealed and whole. The digest refuses before a bound field is read: these are not the bytes the record designates, and comparing against them would be comparing the record against a document it never named.

boundCases.name: bound-mutated-model-id
boundCases.note: The honest record with one bound field moved: the model id names a model the designated manifest does not declare. The refusal names the position and the value, and the record's asserted fields are untouched, which is the difference between the two blocks.

boundCases.name: bound-mutated-weights
boundCases.note: The honest record with the bound weights digest moved to another digest of the same width. The manifest binds one digest per model, and a record stating another is contradicting the document it designates.

boundCases.name: bound-mutated-issuer
boundCases.note: The honest record with the bound issuer moved. The provider is what the manifest signs about itself, and a record naming another issuer beside that manifest's digest is the pair disagreeing about who the deployment is.

boundCases.name: bound-asserted-mutation-accepted
boundCases.note: The honest record with one asserted field moved: the purpose is another statement the deployment could make. Nothing signed covers the purpose, so the verifying door reads it and reports it asserted, while the bound fields still agree with the manifest. This row and the three above are the split's witness: a bound mutation is refused and an asserted mutation is read.

boundCases.name: bound-manifest-without-models
boundCases.note: A record designating a manifest sealed by the same key over a payload with the models member removed. The seal is whole and the digest agrees, and the extraction finds no models to bind against, which is the unreadable refusal rather than a bound disagreement: there is nothing to compare the bound fields to.
